rule: Runbook criterion 12: at no point are more than two lanes live, and no two live lanes own the same (file, symbol) pair per the ownership map -- 'checkable from the map plus the active worktree list'. The map lived only in a section of docs/plans/silent-failure-runbook.md, and an R-35 verifier, whose brief forbids reading the plan, reported the criterion UNVERIFIABLE rather than met: no committed artifact outside the plans recorded lane liveness or (file, symbol) ownership. This file is that artifact, in the shape decision-inventory.json already gives the manifest -- committed, gated, and asserted against the runbook table it is derived from so the two cannot drift.
what_this_can_and_cannot_check: The campaign's history is linear by construction: R-34 rules integration as local-only rebase-then-cherry-pick, never merge, so a lane's concurrency with another is not recoverable from the commit graph. What IS recoverable, and is what this file gates, is the per-lane commit range, the declared concurrency the map allows, and -- for the three files the criterion names as shared by symbol -- every commit that actually wrote to one, attributed to the lane whose range holds it. A writer the map does not list shows up as a divergence row rather than as nothing.

lanes.phase: campaign close and its remediation passes

barrier_order: B0.5 — L6's cast_dependency leaf merged unblocks L1's C6 (the campaign's one backwards edge)
B1 — L1's six corrections unblock L2/L4/L5 and hand ability_spec.py to L2 and champions/syndra.py to L6
B2 — L2 unblocks L3's pairing evidence and hands src/app.py to L4
B3 — L3 unblocks L4's coverage flip
B4 — L4 unblocks L5's amp kernel

shared_by_symbol.carve_out: L1 owns the file outright. L2 and L4 own it as two of "the five hotspots" their rows name, each after its predecessor merged -- sequential handoffs, not concurrent shares. L6 owns only validate_for_champion and the post-parse expansion/check call site, from B1 rather than B0, which is the one carve-out the criterion calls symbol granularity.

L0 owns the DamageClass/AttackClass/Authority/Disposition vocabulary, L1 the 0B consumers, L2 the file from B1, L5 only the Quantity algebra beside Disposition (D-72) as a sequential handoff after L2 merged.
L1 owns the recast_of="Q" stamp only, at C6; L6 owns everything else, from B1.

writers_the_map_does_not_list.what: Phase 4 S5 gives the two narrowed fight results declared readers and repoints the two tuple gates at the ledger projection, which is a pipeline.py edit.
writers_the_map_does_not_list.why_it_is_not_a_criterion_12_violation: L5's row owns program/, survival/*, participant_timeline.py and the two Phase-4 capability fields; it does not name pipeline.py. But L5's range opens at ac1ba4e, after every other lane's range has closed, so no second lane was live -- the map is missing an owner, not describing a collision.

writers_the_map_does_not_list.what: Phase 3's declared zero policy (D-24) lands on ability_spec.py's damage_entry/simple_damage parts, and its follow-up moves the policy off the part's identity.
writers_the_map_does_not_list.why_it_is_not_a_criterion_12_violation: L4 ran alone in the serial chain -- L6, the only lane that may be live beside it, had merged at 146a69c, and L4's range opens at b9c5696 -- so no two LIVE lanes held the file. What it is instead is a map that does not list a real owner, recorded here rather than left as the difference between what the map says and what the tree did.

writers_the_map_does_not_list.what: D-24's source assertion over champions/ -- the guard the declared zero-policy default only holds with -- lands its fixture on Syndra.
writers_the_map_does_not_list.why_it_is_not_a_criterion_12_violation: Same reason: L4's range is disjoint from L6's, so the file was never held by two live lanes.

writers_the_map_does_not_list.what: The R-15/R-18 clause 2 correction for the cast-timeline dissent: Syndra's second Dark Sphere charge stops being free and prices itself off Q's own cached cost row. It is a champions/syndra.py edit.
writers_the_map_does_not_list.why_it_is_not_a_criterion_12_violation: X's row is the close and its remediation passes, and its range opens at 067c94c -- after every phase lane's range has closed -- so no second lane was live and no two lanes held the file. What it is instead is the same shape L4's row above records: the map lists L1 for the recast_of stamp and L6 for the rest, and the lane that re-opened that stamp under clause 2 is neither. Recorded here rather than left as the difference between what the map says and what the tree did.

a_declared_owner_need_not_write: Ownership is permission, not obligation. L1 declares the 0B consumers in ability_spec.py and wrote none in the campaign range; that is a lane not needing what it was allowed, and the gate asserts a subset rather than an equality in that direction. The equality that matters runs the other way: every lane that DID write one of these three files is either a declared owner or a named divergence.
a_later_campaign_is_not_this_map_s: This map's range closes at 7e1de9e, the silent-failure campaign's own tip. The full-coverage campaign that follows writes shared files too — pipeline.py and ability_spec.py among them — but it is not one of these lanes and its writes are not divergences from this map. It carries its own receipt in docs/coverage-census.json.
